To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we propose $^p$-GNN, a new message-passing framework for graph neural networks that can be used for semi-supervised learning on graphs; (2) we provide theoretical analysis that explains why the new message-passing mechanism is effective on homophilic and heterogeneous graphs; and (3) we show experimentally that $^pGNN$ outperforms other state-of-the-art models on several benchmark datasets.
we propose a new message passing mechanism based on $p$-laplacian regularization and spectral analysis.
we propose a new GNN model, named $^p$-GNN, which is effective on both homophlic and heterophlic graphs.

the design of a GNN model which is effective on both homophily and heterophily, which has not been achieved before in the literature.
